 Anwar dismisses claim that minister took RM9.5mil from businessman
 20-Oct-2026, 11:17 20 Oct 2026, 11:17 Dineskumar Ragu Share Prime minister says the accusation is not backed by evidence, and that the minister has taken the matter to court.
 Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said he will not interfere in corruption cases involving members of his own party, PKR. (Bernama pic) 
 KUALA LUMPUR : Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed an allegation that a minister had received RM9.5 million from a businessman. 
 Speaking during a question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat, Anwar said allegations of corruption should be investigated with no exceptions.
 However, he said the RM9.5 million claim was a “political statement” that was “not backed by any evidence”.
 “The minister concerned has challenged it and taken the matter to court,” he said.
 Anwar also said corruption was not confined to any particular political party.
 “If there are cases involving members of PKR, I will not use my powers to stop them, including in the case of my former political secretary,” he said, referring to Shamsul Iskandar Akin who is facing trial for corruption.
 Anwar was responding to Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu), who asked about investigations into so-called corporate mafia activities involving businessman Victor Chin, Farhash Wafa Salvador Rizal Mubarak and former Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief Azam Baki.
 Rosol also referred to an allegation made in a podcast that a minister had received RM9.5 million to act as an intermediary in resolving a corporate mafia-related matter.
 While Anwar did not name the minister, the person accused of receiving RM9.5 million was human resources minister R Ramanan.
 Ramanan has previously denied receiving the sum from Victor Chin, allegedly to help settle the corporate mafia case.
 Anwar also took aim at a former MP “who raised the matter but remained silent when he was serving as a minister”.
 “This is why I tell my friends in Cabinet to use their powers properly to fix things and (not to wait) until they are retired or on the opposition bench to speak up on issues,” he added.
 Separately, Anwar pledged to make public within three months the findings of a special multi-agency task force, led by attorney-general Dusuki Mokhtar, investigating allegations of a corporate mafia.
 He said the task force involved MACC, the police, Bank Negara Malaysia, the Securities Commission, Inland Revenue Board and anti-money laundering enforcement units.
 “It doesn’t matter whether the names mentioned are Azam, Farhash, or Victor Chin,” he said.
 “But let us obtain full disclosure through the special committee headed by the attorney-general.”
 He also said that the police’s anti-money laundering investigation team had frozen RM4.3 billion in funds and seized RM1 billion in assets linked to alleged corporate crimes between late 2022 and September 2026.
 He said enforcement action during the same period also resulted in the forfeiture of RM48.3 million in assets and the issuance of compounds totalling RM1.1 billion.
 He was responding to Aminuddin Harun (PH-Port Dickson), who asked for an update on allegations of “corporate mafia” activities involving violations of the law and the enforcement measures taken against those involved.
